keeper_logbook.title: The keeper’s working book
pages: First clear evening. The lens took all day to clean. By supper the boats were answering from the channel. I watched until the last one passed, though the soup was getting cold.
Water at the third stair again. The printed table says it should be dry. I have cut a new mark beside the old one. For now I am keeping both.
Began the island on the table. One to two hundred and forty, including the crack in the eastern path. The boatwright asked whether I meant to put the draught under the door in it too.
The little valve works. The bay falls when I empty the basin. I called her in to see the road come out of the water. She stayed a long time at the window. I went back to the valve.
deep:
Her question is written below the figures: Where does the water go?

I wrote several answers. None came from going down to look.

signal_shelf.title: The instrument index
pages: Eight small harbour manuals, rubbed pale where they were pulled from the shelf. Each stamped figure belongs to an instrument: sun crank, tide staff, basin wheel, music teeth, stone arc, lamp eye, survey rule, or plumb line.

A pencilled note on the shelf: The bindings are right even where the books are out of date.

The same stamps are cut into the cliff. There are no readings printed here.

coat_letter.title: A letter in the coat
pages: I have put the blue blanket in the east room. The kettle has rainwater in it. The cup with the bent handle is yours if you want it.

You left halfway through telling me about the boat. The bit where you had to start the stern again. I would like to hear the rest.

I will be in when you come back.
deep:
A later line, in softer pencil:

I fixed the latch. You can open it from either side now.

stone_inscription.title: On the standing stone
pages:
WE BUILT THE STEPS WIDE
ENOUGH TO WALK UP TOGETHER
deep:
A smaller cut below the water stain:

THE BOATS ARE TIED ABOVE THE HALL.
BRING THE DOGS FIRST.

bottle_note.title: A note sent by water
pages: If this comes ashore near you, the light is still working. The door below it opens with a lift and a push. It swells in the wet.
I put a very small boat in the east room. There is a split along one side. Please leave it as it is for now. I am trying something.
deep:
The bottle came back.

I sent it out again with a fresh cork. There may still be someone on the other shore.

kelp_slate.title: The boatwright’s wax slate
pages: I saw someone between the weeds and went splashing over. By the time I got there the water was empty. I felt foolish calling out to it.
Next morning I sat on the dry end of the bench. After a while a head came up. We stayed like that. Then it made a low sound, almost a note, and I found I had been holding my breath.

bluff_cairn.title: Pencil under the cairn
pages: He kept appearing nearer whenever I looked at the hall. I thought he wanted me to leave. I put my bag down so I could watch without having to carry it.
He raised his head at last. I had been expecting a face I knew. There was only someone waiting, as wet as I was.

source_note.title: Beside the unfinished boat
pages: This was going to be the good boat. I cut six sterns for it. Each was a little closer to what I had drawn. The first one is under the bench. There is nothing much wrong with it.

She stitched the split with blue thread while I was finding a better piece of wood. It leaks a little. She says we can put it in the shallows and see.

I have left room beside it.

quarters_journal.title: The book beside the pillow
pages: I could hear the wind through the latch, so I put a chair against the door. Later I woke to the sound of the chair moving. It was only the house settling. I stayed awake anyway.
The boatwright brought another chair. Its lower rung is the wrong wood. We sat until the kettle ran dry. I did not once get up to look at the model.
deep:
I moved the first chair back to the table.

The door still rattles. Last night I slept through it.

lens_mark_study.title: Writing beneath the reading glass
pages: She was halfway through a story when the beam touched the cliff. I asked her to wait while I copied the figures. When I looked up she was carrying the cups through to the other room.
The figures return after dark, in the same order. I have left space for them here. I have also left space for the end of her story.
deep: I took the book down to the hall. The ledge where they kept the winter cups was underwater. My own cup was still dry above.

lens_mark_stone.title: On the smooth side of the stone
pages: Thirty-seven shallow strokes, in groups of five. A few have been rubbed smooth by a thumb.

Beside them, small words:

i made this bit smooth so your hand can rest here
deep:
The next line was covered by sand:

there is room for two hands

pool_phial.title: Paper inside the little phial
pages:
A water mark and a date have blurred together. Beneath them, still legible:

Saved from the high pool. The boatwright wanted to know whether it would taste of rain.

A pencilled answer on the folded edge:

It did.

drain_ledger.title: The visitor’s tide ledger
pages: District visit. The keeper’s gauge is accurate. Water stands four centimetres above the table. I have entered the measured figure and asked for the table to be corrected.
Second visit. Eleven centimetres now. The boatwright showed me the wet stair. I said a correction was pending. She asked whether I had brought any dry socks.
deep:
Final visit. The archive floor had flooded before I arrived. We carried the loose sheets upstairs in bread tins. The keeper gave me his spare socks.

I have stopped writing PENDING against the water.

commendation_copy.title: A recommendation, kept
pages:
Recommendation: the light has remained in service through three winters without a missed night. The lens work is exact. The keeper has done the work of a larger station.

I would like this said somewhere he can read it.
deep:
The signature line is empty. Along the bottom, in the keeper’s hand:

I kept waiting for this to make it easier to stop.

closure_notice.title: The proposed closure
pages:
District of Lights. Proposed closure. The light and its instruments may be transferred when a replacement route is established. A response is requested before the next supply boat.

The date has been folded into the crease.
deep:
Across the back, in the boatwright’s hand:

We could have a window that looks at something other than the light. I am only saying we could.

field_slip.title: A field slip under the stone

place.label: a field slip, pinched under stone

pages:
The bluff took me most of the morning. I wrote twenty-two minutes in the return. It was what the last visitor had written.

The boatwright caught up carrying a chair. She did not mention the time.
deep:
Reverse: tower, twenty-one metres; stair, eighty-three treads. Under RELIEF, the keeper has written:

Someone who will stay for supper.

transfer_offer.title: An offer, never burnt

place.label: a letter, wedged behind the stove

pages:
A place is available at the mainland station. Two assistants share the watch. There is a garden behind the house, though the soil needs work.

The visitor has added: I have seen it. There is room.
deep:
An unfinished reply:

I know how to keep this light going. I do not yet know what I would do in the mornings if someone else took a turn.

model_margin.title: In the model’s margin
pages: SCALE 1:240. A pencilled island sits inside the drawn lighthouse. There is another lighthouse on it, and a smaller island on that.
A different hand has added a tiny chair beside the smallest table. It is much too large for the scale.

music_note.title: A note inside the music box
pages:
Fourth tooth catches again. Filed it. Worse.

She laughed when I said I could fix the song. She asked whether the bird had complained.

After filing: E · G · A · D · C.

The bird still answers from the stones at dawn. It waits for the box to finish before it starts.
deep:
Inside the fold:

The bird takes the fourth note higher. We left the window open to hear it again.

spare_place.title: Under the spare chair
pages: This rung came off a different chair. I could have stained it to match. Then I would have had to wait for it to dry, and you were already putting the kettle on.
I will bring the boat tomorrow. We can try it in the basin. There is no need to clear the whole table.

boat_return.title: The little boat
pages: The stitches are still visible along its side. One end sits lower than the other. It has been in the water and come back with a little sand inside.

Under the seat, a word cut into the wood:

Again.

look.3: “There used to be a table there. We all fitted round it.”
look.4: “You can put that down for a while.”

arrive.shallow: “I heard the wheel. Come and see.”
arrive.deep: “I kept making the boat smaller. I thought it might be easier.”

cues.the_sea_no_longer: The sea no longer answers the wheel down here.
cues.the_wheel_turns_and: The wheel turns. The sky follows after a delay.
cues.the_hour_will_not: The wheel turns freely. The sky does not move.
cues.the_register_has_one: The first pages are in the keeper’s hand. Later on, other people took a watch.
cues.the_register_counts_the: {n} different hands have kept this book. Some have left only a line.
cues.the_top_ring_stands: The top ring stands {gap} m clear of the water. Fresh-cut. Nothing has ever reached it.
cues.the_water_is_at: The water is at the fifth ring.
cues.it_has_to_go_somewhere: The lower gauge rises as the upper basin falls.
cues.below_the_window_the: Below the window, the sea obeys.
cues.the_crank_resists_as: The crank is stiff. The sky moves a little after your hand stops.
cues.the_little_lamp_drags: The little lamp drags the real sun with it.
cues.the_fourth_note_does: The fourth tooth catches. The note falls silent.
cues.the_song_comes_up: The song comes up slow and flat, as through water.
cues.fallen_and_long_silent: A stone on its side. A tap gives a dull knock.
cues.the_fallen_stone_hums: The fallen stone now carries the low note heard across the kelp.
cues.the_hinges_remember_how: The lid sticks, then opens with a long creak.
cues.a_cartographer_s_brass: A fifteen-centimetre cartographer’s rule. Brass, straight, unmarked by salt.
cues.across_the_island_something: Across the island, something vast settles into place.
cues.you_do_not_need: The etched marks align with the model’s survey grid.
cues.far_above_glass_settles: Far above, glass settles into brass.
cues.on_the_model_s: On the model beach, a rice-grain bottle is corked around a curl of paper.
cues.even_here_a_staff: A staff the height of an eyelash stands in the model sea. It has five rings; the top is pale.
cues.cold_as_seawater_clear: The lens is cold through your sleeve. A small flaw catches the light.
cues.the_sand_slides_from: The sand slides from a brass door, dialled shut.
cues.stone_breath_long_held: The brass door drops inward. Cold air lifts from a lit stair below.
cues.heavier_than_it_looks: The brass weight pulls the cord vertical.
cues.it_hangs_dead_centre: The plumb hangs over the model beach. The floor plate lies on the same vertical line.
cues.stand_on_it: The brass plate is underfoot beside the table. Move onto its centre to cross.
cues.the_stair_is_roped: The stair is roped off and dark. The lamp socket beside it is empty.
cues.a_line_cut_low: Cut low into the wet stone: “RETURN FLOW +11 SEC.”
cues.locked_not_from_this: The latch turns. The hinges do not move.
cues.glass_and_brass_wedged: Glass and brass are wedged below the dry pool lip, beyond a hand’s reach.
cues.the_bottom_of_the: The bottom of the world, and the pool is finally full. The phial rides the risen water, and your hand closes around it.
cues.a_keeper_s_reading: A keeper’s reading glass. Through it, the faint marks resolve — there is writing everywhere you did not see.
cues.that_is_all_of: Nine lampblack marks found. Their measurements agree.
cues.the_stones_hum_lower: The stones hum lower here, as through water.
cues.e_g_a_d: E, G, A, D, C — with the fallen stone’s lower note beneath them. All six stones sound.
cues.the_stones_refuse_the: The fourth note rings wrong. The dawn bird sang that part differently.
cues.the_outcrop_opens_like: A slab slides into the rock. Behind it, a lens on a dry shelf.
cues.some_corrections_only_ever: The fourth stone answers the higher pitch.
cues.the_bird_sings_the: The bird sings the box’s song. Almost.
cues.the_bay_gives_up: The bay gives up a road of wet stone.
cues.the_lighthouse_remembers_its: The full lighthouse lens seats. Its beam falls through the tower onto the lit model lamp.
cues.the_beam_writes_on: The beam returns four figures from the west cliff.
cues.the_risen_capitals_catch: Four figures reflect from the capitals above the drowned hall, in the same order as the cliff.
cues.far_out_on_the: The beam catches on the drowned hall and holds for one circuit.
cues.a_chart_table_and: The table holds a model of the island. There is a light in its tiny window.
cues.centimetre_marks_underfoot_tall: The ruler marks are taller than you now.
cues.the_dory_and_its: The beached dory holds one unused oar. Its line remains fast to the jetty.
cues.you_set_the_phial: You set the phial from the high pool on the chart table. In the dry air of the study, the little roll of paper loosens from the glass at last.
cues.the_inner_door_stands: The door to the east room is open.
cues.you_have_stood_here: The cup is where you left it. The window is open a little.
cues.another_study_west_of: A facing study contains a drained model basin and a lit model lamp.
cues.a_bell_buoy_listing: A bell-buoy, listing in the drowned channel. It keeps ringing anyway.
cues.you_did_not_run: Under a held gaze, the figure raises its head and breaks into a cold light.
cues.far_along_the_shore: A small cold light stands on the far shore for three breaths, then goes dark.
cues.you_stop_wading_for: When movement stops, the form surfaces and sends one low note across the water.
cues.faint_from_the_kelp: Faint, from the kelp: the note it laid, still crossing the water now and then.
cues.click_and_the_sea: Click, and the sea will hurry.
cues.the_tide_brought_you: The light is on. A path leads up from the beach.
cues.down_is_the_only: The plate’s lower ring is lit. Its upper ring is dark.
cues.there_is_no_level: This is the surface. The east room is through the open door.
cues.you_run_the_mechanism: The room draws smaller. The table above comes into view.
cues.salt_and_lamp_oil: The familiar smell of lamp oil. The kettle has cooled.
cues.far_down_a_light: A light burns in the room below.
cues.there_you_are_a: A lit point appears on the model shore.
cues.everything_down_here_is: Marks below the water line have sharper edges than those above.
cues.the_rope_is_still: A rope swings above the weeds. Someone tied it recently.
cues.the_water_over_the: The water over the hall is moving. Something is coming up.
cues.the_light_passes_under: The light passes under the water — once, all the way around.
cues.the_line_takes_the: The line settles into the cleat’s worn turns.
cues.one_true_line_signed: The observed water level is signed beneath the earlier entries.
cues.the_small_flame_takes: The wick catches. The blue blanket comes into view.
cues.wound_the_way_he: The spring takes one full turn. The cylinder begins to move.
cues.folded_into_my_coat: The folded record fits inside the coat lining.
cues.the_drawer_takes_it: The record rests beside the District returns.
cues.left_with_him_at: Weighted on the source slab, above the wet line.
cues.the_jetty_s_outer: The jetty’s outer arm is a shadow under green water.
cues.the_bench_faces_the: Water washes over the bench seat. There is still a dry place at one end.
cues.the_skiff_is_off: The skiff has lifted off its blocks. Its line is still tied to the old anchor.
cues.field_report_taken_copied: Note sent — position, view, state and a screenshot went with it.

evidence.spare-place.text: The spare chair has a replaced rung. A note underneath invites the keeper to try the boat.

evidence.boat-return.text: The small boat came back with sand inside. Its blue stitches are still visible.

event.place-made.text: I pulled out the spare chair beside the table.

event.boat-launched.text: I set the stitched boat in the basin. It floats with one end a little low.

arrival.shallows.text: The shallows are higher. Kelp crosses the old footpath.

arrival.inspection.text: Water reaches the drowned hall roof. The study window is below the tide line.

arrival.source.text: The fifth gauge ring is wet. The upper stone pool is full.

return.receiver.text: Back from the shallows. The lamp is still burning in the east room.

return.surface.text: Back at the original study. The east room is above the changed waterline.

evidence.model-marker.text: A moving point on the table model matches my position on the island.

event.refuge-lit.text: The cot lamp is lit. The east room is dry.

evidence.valve.text: Turning the brass valve lowers the model basin and the bay together.

evidence.music-box.text: The music box plays E · G · A · D · C. Its fourth tooth has been filed twice.

evidence.ruler.text: The brass ruler spans the crack in the model. A measured bridge now spans the eastern chasm.

evidence.lens.text: The small lens fits the model lighthouse. The full lighthouse lens turns with it.

evidence.bird.text: At dawn the bird sings five notes. Its fourth note is higher than the music box’s.

evidence.beam-glyphs.label: copied from the cliff
evidence.beam-glyphs.text: Four figures returned in the lighthouse beam. I copied their order.

artifact.signal-shelf.surface.label: copied from the instrument index
artifact.signal-shelf.surface.text: Eight stamped figures each point to a different working instrument. The spines print names, not values.

evidence.hatch-numerals.text: The buried hatch has four numeral wheels and the same figure stamps as the manuals.

evidence.shadow-hatch.text: At golden hour the five standing stones cast one joined shadow toward the buried hatch.

evidence.plumb.text: The plumb hangs over the model beach. A brass plate lies at the corresponding point in the study floor.

evidence.tide-gauge.text: The gauge has five rings. The first four cuts are weathered; the fifth is pale and sharp.

evidence.dead-wheel.text: Below the surface, the full-sized valve is locked. Salt prints ring its wheel; the model counterpart is free.

evidence.fallen-stone.text: Five stones stand in an arc. A sixth lies face down and gives only a dull knock.

event.upstream-hand.text: With the lower wheel still, the water rose by one hand’s width. Salt handprints remain on the wheel.

evidence.register.text: The register records work at this table before and after the keeper’s entries. Several hands did not sign.

encounter.tide-figure.text: When I stopped advancing, the form held together and surfaced. It left one low note across the bay.

encounter.watcher.text: The shore figure advanced only while unobserved. Under a held gaze it raised its head and dispersed.

encounter.lower-hand.text: The lower study bears the results of changes made above: wet steps, a raised basin, and another hand’s measurements.

event.capitals-breach.text: Three inscribed crowns rose through the water over the drowned hall.

event.beam-farewell.text: At the source, the beam completed one submerged circuit and went dark.

evidence.room-disagreement.text: The facing study’s model shows a drained bay and lit lamp not present in this room.

evidence.bell-buoy.text: The buoy still marks its old channel, now beneath the flooded bluff.

evidence.crank.text: The model lamp crank changes the sky’s hour. The mechanism lags at greater depth.

evidence.model-bottle.text: A sealed bottle rests on the model beach. A smaller curl of paper is visible inside.

evidence.model-gauge.text: A five-ring gauge stands beside the model sea. Its top ring is pale.

evidence.climber-rope.text: A tied climbing rope is still moving at the wade line; its lower end is submerged.

mechanism.stone-vault.text: The stone arc opened a chamber in the outcrop. A fitted lens lay inside.

mechanism.lighthouse.text: With the model lens seated, the full lighthouse beam follows the model housing.

mechanism.reading-glass.text: The reading glass resolves lampblack marks invisible to the unaided eye.

event.fifth-ring.text: Water has reached the fifth gauge ring for the first recorded time.

event.returned-shore.text: After the ascent, the outer jetty arm, shallows bench, and skiff are underwater.

evidence.study-model.text: The study model matches the island at one to two hundred and forty, including this room.

evidence.study-unchanged.text: On return, the cup, chair, dust, and clock hand occupy their earlier positions.

collection.climber.cmTallies.text: Thirty-seven short strokes in groups of five; a palm-wide hollow beside them.

collection.climber.cmFormal.text: “I CAME DOWN LATE. THEY MADE A PLACE FOR ME.”

collection.climber.cmPlain.text: “left my coat on the third stair. anyone can have it.”

collection.climber.cmUnfinished.text: “day nine below. more tea, less measuring” — the cut ends mid-line.

collection.climbers-complete.text: Five distinct hands appear at five depths. None is listed in the station log.

collection.hall.cgRoof.text: “WE MADE THE TABLE LONGER EACH WINTER.” Water now stands above it.

collection.hall.cgCount.text: “WE COUNTED OURSELVES EACH WINTER —” The number is effaced.

collection.hall.cgLight.text: “WHEN WE MOVED UPHILL WE TOOK THE TABLE.”

collection.hall-complete.text: All three hall inscriptions use the same plural hand.

collection.lampblack.lmValve.text: TEST 6 — upper basin minus 9; lower basin plus 9.

collection.lampblack.lmBox.text: Fourth tooth filed twice. Pitch fell both times.

collection.lampblack.lmChest.text: Seal held through three spring tides.

collection.lampblack.lmDory.text: Hull sound. One oar missing before inventory.

collection.lampblack.lmStair.text: Eighty-three treads. Third wet at neap.

collection.lampblack.lmBell.text: Toll carries farther below the water line.

collection.lampblack.lmBuoy.text: Mooring datum no longer marks the channel.

collection.lampblack-complete.text: Nine lampblack measurements appear on working objects across the island.

event.round.moor.text: The dory line is made fast at the jetty cleat.

event.round.log.text: The day’s return is signed with the observed water level.

event.round.light.text: The cot lamp is lit. The model lighthouse answers briefly.

event.round.wind.text: The music box is wound once. A bird remains at the sill through all five notes.

event.rounds-complete.text: Mooring, return, cot lamp, and music box have each been tended once.

evidence.completed-song.text: The standing stones accept six notes when the fallen stone carries the added low tone.

evidence.disposition.text: The mechanism can hold, reverse, join, or seal the transfer. Each changes both sides of the plate.

evidence.logbook.surface.text: The keeper built a working model. The boatwright watched the water leave the bay.

evidence.logbook.deep.text: The boatwright asked where the water went. The keeper wrote answers before going down to look.

evidence.coat-letter.surface.text: The boatwright left a blanket, a cup and an invitation to finish a story.

evidence.coat-letter.deep.text: The latch was repaired so the door opens from either side.

evidence.standing-stone.surface.text: The first settlers built the steps wide enough to walk up together.

evidence.standing-stone.deep.text: The lower inscription says the boats are above the hall and the dogs should go first.

evidence.bottle.surface.text: A note gives directions to the light. It mentions a small split boat left in the east room.

evidence.bottle.deep.text: The bottle returned and was sent out again with a fresh cork.

evidence.kelp-slate.surface.text: The boatwright lost the figure by approaching. Sitting on the bench, she heard its low note.

evidence.bluff-cairn.surface.text: The visitor watched the shore figure after putting down the bag. It raised its head.

evidence.transfer-sheet.surface.text: The keeper made six sterns. The boatwright stitched the split with blue thread.

evidence.quarters-journal.surface.text: The keeper blocked the door with a chair. Later the boatwright brought another chair.

evidence.quarters-journal.deep.text: The keeper moved the chair back to the table and slept through the rattling door.

evidence.lens-study.surface.text: The keeper interrupted a story to copy the beam. Space remains for both on the page.

evidence.lens-study.deep.text: The keeper found the winter cup ledge flooded in the lower hall.

evidence.lens-stone.surface.text: Beside the tallies, someone smoothed a place for a hand.

evidence.lens-stone.deep.text: The covered line says there is room for two hands.

evidence.pool-phial.surface.text: The paper records water from the high pool. The boatwright said it tasted of rain.

evidence.drain-ledger.surface.text: The visitor recorded rising water. The boatwright asked whether the visitor had dry socks.

evidence.drain-ledger.deep.text: The archive flooded. They carried sheets upstairs in bread tins.

evidence.commendation.surface.text: A visitor recommended recognition for the keeper’s uninterrupted work.

evidence.commendation.deep.text: The keeper hoped recognition would make it easier to stop.

evidence.closure.surface.text: The District proposed closure when a replacement route was established.

evidence.closure.deep.text: The boatwright suggested a window facing away from the light.

evidence.field-slip.surface.text: The visitor copied an earlier walking time. The boatwright arrived carrying a chair.

evidence.field-slip.deep.text: The keeper wrote that relief could mean someone who stayed for supper.

evidence.transfer-offer.surface.text: A mainland station offered shared watches and a garden.

evidence.transfer-offer.deep.text: An unfinished reply wonders what the keeper would do if someone else took a watch.

evidence.model-margin.surface.text: Someone drew a spare chair beside the smallest table. It exceeds the scale.

evidence.music-note.surface.text: The fourth tooth was filed. The bird waits for the box to finish before answering.

evidence.music-note.deep.text: The bird raises the fourth note. The window was left open to hear it again.

ending.tend.text: The transfer is held at its present level. The lamp continues to turn.

ending.open.text: The basins are joined. Their water levels move toward one another.

ending.close.text: The plate is sealed. Pressure falls to zero on the upper side and remains below.

climbers.whisper: Thirty-seven short strokes, grouped by five. The stone is smooth beside them.
An old formal hand, every letter ruled straight: “I CAME DOWN LATE. THEY MADE A PLACE FOR ME.”
A plain hand on the stone: “left my coat on the third stair. anyone can have it.”
A hurried hand, low on the cairn: “day nine below. more tea, less measuring” — and it stops.
Small letters, close to the cold floor, in a hand still learning its letters: “i can hear you up there”

lampblack.place: the drain wall, beside the carved line
